title: Paramedic Salary Perth: Hourly Rates, Casual Loading, and Super Explained
description: Discover how to calculate a paramedic salary in Perth using award rates, casual loading, and super. Use our hourly-to-annual tool for accurate estimates.
salarySummary: A paramedic in Perth covered by the Ambulance and Patient Transport Industry Award earns a minimum hourly rate set by the award; assuming 38 hours per week, the annual gross is hourly rate × 38 × 52, with 25% casual loading and 12% super paid on top.

faqs.q: What is the typical hourly rate for a paramedic in Perth?
faqs.a: Paramedics in Perth are covered by the Ambulance and Patient Transport Industry Award 2020. Minimum hourly rates vary by classification (e.g., trainee, qualified, advanced). For current minimum rates, refer to the Fair Work Ombudsman’s pay guide for that award. Many employers pay above the award, but no single survey figure is authoritative. Use our [pay guides](/blog) to find the latest award rates.

faqs.q: How does casual loading affect a paramedic salary in Perth?
faqs.a: Casual employees under the award receive a 25% loading on top of the base hourly rate. For example, if the base rate is $30.00 per hour, the casual rate becomes $37.50 per hour. This loading compensates for entitlements like paid leave. Use our [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) page to see how it changes your annual estimate.

faqs.q: Is superannuation included in the advertised hourly rate for paramedics?
faqs.a: No. Superannuation is paid on top of your ordinary earnings. The current super guarantee rate is 12% of your ordinary time earnings, up to the maximum contribution base ($270,830 in 2026–27). So if your hourly rate is $35.00, your employer pays an additional $4.20 per hour into your super fund. See [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) for more details.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding a Paramedic Salary in Perth

If you are researching a **paramedic salary in Perth**, the most reliable starting point is the minimum pay rates set by the Fair Work Commission’s Ambulance and Patient Transport Industry Award. This award covers paramedics employed by state ambulance services and private patient transport providers. While actual salaries can vary based on experience, qualifications, and employer, the award provides a legal floor.

### How to Convert an Hourly Rate to Annual Pay

The standard formula used on this site is:

**Annual gross pay = hourly rate × hours per week × 52**

We assume a full‑time week of 38 hours, which is the ordinary hours under the award. For example, if a paramedic’s base hourly rate is $30.00:

- Weekly pay = $30.00 × 38 = $1,140.00
- Fortnightly pay = $1,140.00 × 2 = $2,280.00
- Annual gross = $30.00 × 38 × 52 = $59,280.00

This calculation assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, and no allowances. It is a starting estimate.

### Casual Loading and Superannuation

Many paramedics work on a casual basis. The award requires a 25% casual loading on the base rate. So a $30.00 base rate becomes $37.50 per hour for casuals. When using our [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) tool, tick the casual loading checkbox to add 25% on top of the base rate you enter. **Do not** enter a rate that already includes casual loading.

Superannuation is paid on top of your ordinary earnings. The current super guarantee is 12% of your ordinary time earnings, up to the maximum contribution base ($270,830 for 2026–27). Using the $30.00 base rate example, your employer contributes an extra $3.60 per hour ($30.00 × 12%) into your super fund. This is not deducted from your take‑home pay.

### Award Rates vs National Minimum Wage

The National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour (or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours). Casual employees get $33.05 per hour including the 25% loading. However, paramedics are covered by a specific award, which almost always sets higher minimum rates. Always check the Fair Work Ombudsman’s [pay guides](/blog) for the Ambulance and Patient Transport Industry Award to see the correct classification rates.

### Tax and Take‑Home Pay

Once you have your annual gross estimate, you can work out your approximate take‑home pay using the 2026–27 resident tax rates:

- $0 – $18,200: nil
- $18,201 – $45,000: 15% on excess over $18,200
- $45,001 – $135,000: 30% on excess over $45,000
- $135,001 – $190,000: 37% on excess over $135,000
- Over $190,000: 45% on excess over $190,000

Plus the Medicare levy of 2% (using the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds as the 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed here). No HELP or Medicare levy surcharge is deducted in this estimate. Use our [take‑home pay](/topics/take-home) page for a more detailed calculator.

### Fortnightly and Weekly Comparisons

Knowing your fortnightly pay is helpful for budgeting. Simply multiply your weekly pay by two. For a $30.00 base rate paramedic:

- Weekly: $1,140.00
- Fortnightly: $2,280.00
- Annual: $59,280.00

If casual loading applies, the weekly figure becomes $1,425.00 ($37.50 × 38) and the fortnightly $2,850.00.

### Where to Find Current Paramedic Pay Rates

The Fair Work Commission publishes the Modern Awards Pay Database, which includes classification rates, allowances, and penalty rates for the Ambulance and Patient Transport Industry Award. The Fair Work Ombudsman also provides easy‑to‑read pay guides. For the most accurate **paramedic salary in Perth**, combine these official sources with your specific employment offer.

Remember that the Australian Taxation Office has a dedicated guide for paramedics covering income and work‑related deductions. Claiming legitimate expenses can reduce your taxable income.

### Important Disclaimer

The annual pay shown here is an estimate only. It assumes a constant hourly rate, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax uses the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax‑free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. Always consult a qualified professional for your personal situation.

For more tools, see our [reference tables](/data) and [about the timesheet](/about) page.
